text:
maria_finance: Heads-up — ZenHealth flagged invoice INV-2024-0719, saying the burst/overage charges look incorrect. They were billed $3,200 for Jun 12 burst; they claim platform downtime should have triggered SLA credit.

sam_sales: added context — ZenHealth had a reserved Dedicated pool (3xA100 equiv) with a monthly commit of $14,000. On Jun 12 they had a traffic spike and used burst capacity for ~7.5 hours.

lee_csm: customer says they experienced latency/timeouts between 11:05-13:30 UTC that day. They opened a ticket with support (CASE-9981) and attached logs. CSM uploaded the support thread here: https://redwood.at/support/CASE-9981 :disappointed:

olivia_ops: checked infra dashboard — there was a region-level failover at 11:07 caused by an autoscaler bug; we failed over to secondary region and some requests saw >5s tails for ~2.1 hours. Total platform downtime (partial degradation) logged: 2.1h.

billing-bot: Invoice INV-2024-0719: Reserved commit charge = $14,000; Usage overage (burst) = $3,200; SLA credit applied = $0; Total = $17,200.

maria_finance: Customer argues per our SLA they should get credits for the degraded period. Need clarification: do we issue credit against the $3.2k overage, or a separate SLA credit line? Also need GL/AR impact for revenue ops.

aaron_revenueops: Quick calc request: what credit % applies? SLA doc: "Partial degradation >2h and <4h -> 10% credit of monthly Dedicated fee". If that's right, 10% of $14,000 = $1,400. We could apply $1,400 credit to their account.

sam_sales: ZenHealth specifically asked for the burst fees to be removed, not just a general credit. They're worried about the spike being induced by our failover. They want $3,200 removed.

lee_csm: customer is live with several clinical workflows; maintaining goodwill matters. We should propose the 10% monthly credit plus a one-time goodwill waiver for the burst charge?

olivia_ops: ops accepts responsibility for the failover root cause. From infra POV the burst was partially our fault. I support waiving the overage. Need finance sign-off for write-off.

maria_finance: two options: (A) Apply SLA credit of $1,400 to invoice and keep overage (customer pays $15,800), or (B) waive overage $3,200 + apply SLA credit $1,400 = total concession $4,600 and invoice becomes $12,600. Accounting note: waiving overage is a direct revenue adjustment; SLA credit can be recorded as contractual credit. We need approval from RevOps for Option B write-off.

aaron_revenueops: I can approve up to $5k one-off concessions without exec sign-off if Ops signs root-cause. olivia_ops, can you add short RCA summary in CASE-9981? I'll need it for audit.

olivia_ops: will add RCA by EOD. Short version: autoscaler race condition -> region failover -> increased tail latency -> burst usage. Logging & fix PR linked.

maria_finance: Ping @aaron_revenueops for approval to apply Option B (waive overage + SLA credit). If approved, I'll update invoice and issue corrected invoice PDF and credit memo. Also need to mark in billing system for revenue recognition.

aaron_revenueops: Approved. Please proceed with Option B. Record as: concession_type=one_time_writeoff, amount=$3,200;sla_credit=$1,400;total_concession=$4,600. I will note in RevOps ledger.

maria_finance: Thanks — will push corrected invoice and credit memo. Draft message to customer: "Thanks for raising this — we've applied a $4,600 concession (includes SLA credit) and issued a corrected invoice INV-2024-0719-C. We're sorry for the disruption; ops has a corrective plan." Will share thread for sign-off before sending.

sam_sales: Customer-facing OK from my side. Suggest adding a 1-month free burst buffer (trial) to restore trust.

lee_csm: I'll include the trial in the message.

maria_finance: Draft sent to this thread for final checks. Will update AR when credit memo posts.

billing-bot: Credit memo CM-2024-334 created. Corrected invoice INV-2024-0719-C issued.

lee_csm: Customer replied: "> Thank you — appreciate the quick resolution and the trial. Looking forward to the RCA." :thumbsup:
